Anthony Burden Auburn LD 145
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and distinguished members of the Taxation Committee,
My name is Anthony Burden, Director of Medical Supplies at Bedard Pharmacy and Medical Supplies in Auburn, Maine. Our 110+ employees are dedicated to providing critical medical equipment and supplies to residents across the state.
We strongly support LD 145, which comprehensively addresses the taxation of medical equipment and supplies. This bill aligns with existing exemptions in Maine Revenue Services Instructional Bulletin NO. 41, recognizing the essential nature of medical supplies for Maine residents' health and well-being.
Currently, the sales tax imposes financial and administrative burdens on us for durable medical equipment and supply items that are not currently tax exempt, especially since MaineCare and other insurers do not always reimburse this expense. Removing this taxation will allow us to continue reinvesting in our services for the community through increased product offerings and coverage area.
We thank you for your support on this bill and for supporting the care of everyone across the state.
Anthony Burden Director of Medical Supplies Bedard Pharmacy & Medical Supplies

February 3, 2025
The Honorable Senator Nicole Grohoski Co-Chair, Joint Committee on Taxation Maine State House Room 127 2 State House Station August, Maine 04333
The Honorable Representative Kristen Cloutier Co-Chair, Joint Committee on Taxation Maine State House Room 127 2 State House Station August, Maine 04333
RE: Support for LD 145 - Pertaining to Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Durable Medical Equipment, Breast Pumps and Mobility-enhancing Equipment
Dear Co-Chairs Grohoski and Cloutier:
On behalf of the Consumer Healthcare Products Association (CHPA), the national trade association representing the leading manufacturers of over-the-counter (OTC) medicines, dietary supplements, and OTC medical devices, I'm writing to express strong support for LD 145. This legislation expands access to critical medical devices for new parents by eliminating the existing sales and use tax associated with their sale.
Breast pumps are essential medical devices that allow parents to extract and store breast milk for their infants, particularly crucial for working parents who need to return to work before the recommended breastfeeding period ends. These devices support optimal infant health outcomes, as breastfeeding reduces risks of various conditions including asthma and diabetes according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), while the National Institutes of Health (NIH) reports that low breastfeeding rates add over $3 billion annually to U.S. medical costs. Despite infant formula being tax-exempt in most states, breast pumps and related supplies remain taxable, creating a financial barrier particularly for lowincome families - an issue that could be addressed through tax policy reform.
Maine families rely on breast milk pumps and supplies as essential items for infant care. By eliminating sales tax on these products, LD 145 would help make them more accessible and affordable for residents across the state. We applaud Senator Rotundo's leadership in introducing this legislation and urge the Joint Committee on Taxation to vote in favor of passage.
Respectfully submitted,

Carlos I. Gutierrez Vice President, State & Local Government Affairs Consumer Healthcare Products Association cgutierrez@chpa.org | 202-429-3521 Cc: Joint Committee on Taxation
The Honorable Senator Peggy Rotundo

TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: Tuesday, February 4, 2025, at 1:00 P.M.
LD 145 - "An Act Pertaining to Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Durable Medical Equipment, Breast Pumps and Mobility-enhancing Equipment"
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration in Support of LD 145, "An Act Pertaining to Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Durable Medical Equipment, Breast Pumps and Mobility-enhancing Equipment."
LD 145 would provide a broader and simpler sales and use tax exemption for durable medical equipment ("DME"), breast pumps, and mobility-enhancing equipment for home use or use in a motor vehicle. The exemptions and definitions proposed in this bill were included in the Governor's Supplemental Budget during the 131st Legislature and are included in the Governor's current Biennial Budget proposal, specifically within Part G of that document. LD 145 as printed would require some minor technical edits due to amendments made in the last Legislative session that shifted Maine's sales tax to the "lease stream" model, generally treating each lease or rental payment as a separate taxable sale and correspondingly extending the general sale for resale exclusion. That shift to the lease stream was considered in detail last Session by the 131st Legislature and was enacted both as part of the 2nd Session Supplement Budget (P.L. 2023, c.643) and LD 2000 (P.L. 2023, c.673). The combination of the DME exemption under LD 145 now before
1

this Committee and the lease stream changeover enacted last Session will simplify taxpayer understanding and compliance with respect to sales and rentals of durable medical equipment.
The preliminary fiscal impact for the bill is a revenue loss of $250,000 per year.
The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

Testimony in Support of LD 145
"An Act Pertaining to Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Durable Medical Equipment, Breast Pumps and Mobility Enhancing Equipment"
"Presented to the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation February 4, 2025

Good afternoon Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and the members of the Joint Standing

Committee on Taxation. My name is Peggy Rotundo. I have the distinct pleasure of representing the
people of the City of Lewiston in Senate District 21. I am here today to introduce LD 145, "An Act

Pertaining to the Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Durable Medical Equipment, Breast Pumps and

Mobility Enhancing Equipment."

-

Being able to afford medical care is a struggle for many Maine families. It requires navigating a
complex, at times, unreliable health insurance system, and treatment and equipment costs can result
in major financial burdens for Maine families. During a 2021 survey, almost 80% of Mainers
expressed concerns about being able to afford future medical care, and more than half of Maine adults said they had skipped, delayed, or avoided medical treatment because of costs. I feel strongly that it is our job as lawmakers to pursue any and all possible solutions to make healthcare more
affordable and accessible to working people. This bill I am presenting to you is a step in the right
direction.

This legislation would exempt prescribed medical equipment from both sales and use tax. Prescribed

medical equipment is equipment that is required to manage certain health conditions, such as

nebulizers, insulin pumps, and other long tenn home use devices. This equipment is often referred to

as "durable medical equipment (DME)." Access to these items can offer greater consistency when

treating illnesses, therefore improving the patient's quality of life. In Maine, this equipment is

currently subject to taxes that the medications for these conditions are not. Other equipment like

mobility devices such as prosthetics and wheelchairs, as well as diabetic supplies and oxygen

delivery equipment, is exempt from these taxes.

.

Enacting a tax exemption on DME would improve access and make it more affordable for all
Mainers, especially those struggling with payments, or avoiding treatment for fear of exorbitant

Dear Chairman Young and Esteemed Members of the House Finance Committee,
My name is Ryan Bullock, Chief Strategy Officer of Aeroflow Health, and l am writing in strong support
of LD 145, which seeks to eliminate the sales tax on durable medical equipment and breast pumps. This bill is a necessary step toward making essential medical and healthcare products more affordable for Maine residents who rely on them for their well-being and daily functioning.
Durable medical equipment (DME), such as wheelchairs, walkers, and oxygen tanks, is not optional for
those who need it----it is vital to their independence, mobility, and quality of life. For individuals with disabilities, seniors, and those managing chronic illnesses, the additional cost of sales tax on these necessary devices creates an undue financial burden, particularly for those on fixed or limited incomes. Removing this tax would help ensure that all Mainers have equitable access to the equipment they
need without unnecessary financial hardship.
Similarly, breast pumps are a critical tool for new parents, supporting infant nutrition, maternal health, and breastfeeding success. The cost of these devices can already be prohibitive for many families and taxing them only adds to the financial stress faced by parents. By exempting breast pumps from sales
tax, Maine would be promoting public health and supporting families in their choice to provide optimal
nutrition for their infants.
l_D 145 represents a compassionate and practical approach to public policy--one that prioritizes accessibility, health, and economic fairness. I urge you to support and pass this bill to remove
unnecessary financial barriers for those who need these essential medical supplies.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
